quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report: H1 2026 consolidated revenue KRW 28,761,869,907 versus KRW 40,243,311,444 in H1 2025, with an H1 operating loss of KRW 6,330,336,323 (H1 2025: operating profit KRW 5,990,582,188). Q2 2026 revenue KRW 20,832,585,957 (Q2 2025: KRW 23,159,312,598) with a Q2 operating loss of KRW 786,341,945 (Q2 2025: profit KRW 2,578,412,351). H1 net loss KRW 1,180,596,118.

Product mix, H1 2026: equipment sales KRW 18,827M (65.5% of revenue), of which AEGIS-II front-end patterned-wafer inspection KRW 12,623M and KROKY HBM inspection KRW 5,865M, all domestic; services (setup, repair, wafer inspection) KRW 9,846M (34.2%), of which China KRW 6,428M. No equipment was exported to China in H1 (FY2025: KRW 12,214M; FY2024: KRW 88,357M), and China revenue fell to KRW 6,427,887,143 from KRW 11,529,611,897 in H1 2025. In FY2025 KROKY was KRW 27,970M or 60.0% of equipment revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: equipment KRW 18,827M (AEGIS-II KRW 12,623M, KROKY KRW 5,865M); services KRW 9,846M; China revenue KRW 6,427,887,143 (H1 2025 KRW 11,529,611,897)

quarterly_data.signal: KROKY HBM inspection: Nextin says KROKY has been applied on mass-production lines from 12-high HBM3E, detecting warpage-related chipping and cracks at die edges that other global tools could not, and that it is the only commercial tool supporting 12-high HBM3E inspection; it began supplying domestic HBM lines in 2025. The company expects KROKY use to widen with higher HBM stack counts and advanced-packaging inspection demand, including supply to new global chipmakers beyond its existing HBM customer.
quarterly_data.figure: KROKY on mass-production lines from 12-high HBM3E

quarterly_data.signal: Order backlog for wafer inspection systems was KRW 8,978M at June 30, 2026 (KRW 7,736M at end-2025), with KRW 21,012M of new orders and KRW 19,770M delivered in H1 2026. Nextin notes that customers usually issue purchase orders only 1-2 months before delivery, so long-range backlog is hard to compile.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog KRW 8,978M; H1 orders KRW 21,012M; H1 deliveries KRW 19,770M

quarterly_data.signal: Customer concentration: customer A accounted for KRW 16,910,196,734 of H1 2026 consolidated revenue, a ratio of 0.5879 (H1 2025: KRW 28,220,447,195, ratio 0.7012), and customer B KRW 4,412,490,000, ratio 0.1534; the note does not name them. The business section lists Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Magnachip in Korea and YMTC and SMIC in China among buyers of its inspection tools.
quarterly_data.figure: customer A KRW 16,910,196,734 (ratio 0.5879); customer B KRW 4,412,490,000 (ratio 0.1534)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex: Nextin has annual capacity of 60 to 70 tools (about three months to build each), in a 1,339.8 m2 clean room plus a leased 1,089 m2 external clean room. H1 2026 cash paid for PP&E was KRW 15,284,250,332; buildings rose to KRW 31,832M as KRW 19,513M moved from construction in progress. It has paid KRW 14,846,687,100 of a KRW 16,496,319,000 contract for industrial-complex land in Yongin (Wonsam-myeon) for manufacturing expansion, with registration due 2027-12-31. Planned R&D capex includes a high-speed in-line X-ray inspection tool (KRW 6,571M, 2026-2029) and SWIR (KRW 3,000M, 2026-2028).
quarterly_data.figure: capacity 60-70 tools per year; H1 PP&E acquisitions KRW 15,284,250,332; Yongin land contract KRW 16,496,319,000

quarterly_data.signal: R&D: H1 2026 R&D spending KRW 6,228M (21.65% of revenue, versus 16.15% in FY2025), with 55 R&D staff including 10 at its Israeli image-processing lab. Development programmes include GENiS, a 266nm DUV bright-field patterned-defect inspection tool with 1x-nm sensitivity aimed at entering the DUV bright-field market, and a front-end static-charge removal tool for EUV and fine processes (to 2026-12). Main raw materials bought in H1 were mechanical parts KRW 8,352M, optical parts KRW 4,602M and machined parts KRW 2,739M.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 R&D KRW 6,228M (21.65% of revenue); H1 raw-material purchases KRW 15,866M

contracts.signal: The half-year report's supply-contract table lists a Wafer Inspection System KROKY supply contract with SK Hynix first disclosed 2026-03-26, running 2026-03-26 to 2026-10-11, 60% complete at June 30, 2026 with KRW 6,364M supplied. Earlier KROKY contracts with SK Hynix (KRW 6,383M from 2025-04-28 and KRW 10,638M from 2025-05-21) and a KRW 5,700M wafer inspection system contract from 2024-12-23 are complete.
